evidence_quotes.quote: This paper provides a Panarctic review of the regulations, loads, and treatment of wastewater (WW) discharged in the Arctic region.

To accomplish this, we surveyed and compiled national and international WW regulations, reports and statistics, and reviewed literature to identify challenges and best practices regarding WWT in the Arctic and its environmental impacts.

As for the evaluation of fraction and level of treatment per country, exact data were available for many of the countries while for others, assumptions based on our literature review combined with the information about legislative requirements and the Author's general familiarity with the region were made.
In many parts of the region, authorities have issued waivers and exemptions to national legislation due to special Arctic conditions.

Overall, in the Arctic region, preliminary, primary, secondary, and tertiary treatment levels are accomplished for approximately 22, 39, 16 and 3% of total WW, respectively. This leaves 20% of the total WW untreated or unknown.

criterion_notes.c1: Fails C1. The paper examines environmental domestic wastewater treatment technologies, effluent quality standards, pollutant/Population Equivalent (PE) loads discharged into Arctic receiving waters, sludge disposal, and aquatic ecosystem impacts rather than household or community access to water or sanitation services. Brief mentions of sewers, septic tanks, or bucket toilets serve only as background to estimate treated vs. untreated environmental discharge loads (many untreated discharges come from piped urban sewer outfalls to the ocean).
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording vs. narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading: Under the plain literal wording of Criterion 2 in isolation, the paper describes legal, regulatory, and institutional factors (national/territorial wastewater effluent regulations, environmental permitting, MARPOL vessel rules, and cold-climate/ocean-outfall waivers), though the overall paper decision under the plain reading is still exclude (plain_criterion2_decision = exclude) because it fails C1, C3, C4, and C5. Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading, it fails C2 (no) because the laws reviewed are environmental pollution-control and effluent-quality standards governing wastewater discharge into receiving waters rather than rule-type mechanisms directly governing household or community service access (brief single-sentence mentions of mandatory sewer connection within network areas in Finland/Norway and age/dwelling exemptions for rural on-site treatment in Finland are unanalysed descriptive background).
criterion_notes.c3: Fails C3. Published as a narrative Critical Review with no primary empirical data collection and no systematic review methodology (no search strategy, databases, or study eligibility criteria). Its quantitative overview compiles secondary official statistics, permit documents, informal inquiries to authorities, and broad author assumptions to estimate aggregate Population Equivalent wastewater treatment shares.
criterion_notes.c4: Fails C4. Reports aggregate Population Equivalent (PE) wastewater loads by treatment technology and effluent treatment level (preliminary, primary, secondary, tertiary, untreated), plant compliance with effluent standards, sludge management, and receiving-water ecological/antibiotic-resistance impacts—not household or community sanitation service access, connection, reliability, quantity, affordability, or exclusion.
criterion_notes.c5: Fails C5. As a non-systematic critical review and descriptive regional wastewater-load inventory, there is no identifiable empirical study design evaluating the effect of a legal or administrative exposure on a household or community service-access outcome.
criterion_notes.c6: Passes C6. Full text is written in English.

study_design: Critical review (non-systematic narrative review) and descriptive regional inventory of secondary wastewater treatment statistics
country: Arctic region (United States [Alaska], Canada, Faroe Islands, Finland, Greenland, Iceland, Norway, Russia, Sweden, and Arctic cruise-ship waters)
population_and_sample: Domestic wastewater loads across the Panarctic region covering 9 jurisdictions plus cruise ships (approximately 5.2 million inhabitants in Population Equivalents compiled from secondary census/utility databases, authority inquiries, and author estimates)
exposure: Environmental wastewater discharge regulations, effluent quality limits, recipient-sensitivity criteria, and cold-climate/ocean-outfall waivers across Arctic jurisdictions (descriptive overview only; no household service-access exposure tested)
outcome: Aggregate Population Equivalent (PE) domestic wastewater loads by treatment technology and effluent treatment level (preliminary, primary, secondary, tertiary, untreated), sludge disposal practices, and receiving-water ecological and antibiotic-resistance impacts
rationale: The retrieved full text matches Record R33EDCF0902FE (Jensen et al., 2025, DOI: 10.1039/d5va00082c). Exclude as E01 (Wrong topic): this article is an environmental science Critical Review of wastewater treatment technologies, effluent pollution loads, environmental discharge regulations (BOD/TSS/nutrient limits, MARPOL ship rules, ocean-outfall waivers), sludge disposal, and aquatic ecosystem/antibiotic-resistance impacts in the Arctic, rather than a study of household or community water or sanitation service access. In addition, under the 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 clarification, it examines environmental pollution-control standards rather than rule-type mechanisms governing service access, and it is a non-systematic review plus descriptive secondary-data/assumption-based PE load inventory with no empirical evaluation of a service-access outcome (so plain_criterion2_decision is also exclude).
